paper.title_en: NRHJSur3dq8: a spectral numerical-relativity surrogate family for non-eccentric aligned-spin binary-black-hole waveforms
paper.abstract_en: We present NRHJSur3dq8, a family of numerical-relativity surrogates for non-eccentric aligned-spin binary-black-hole waveforms inspired by an action-angle parameterization. The model provides both the dynamics: the Hamiltonian values, azimuthal action $J_φ(Φ)$, the orbital clock $τ(Φ)$ as functions of its phasing, and the radiative pieces: the waveforms, their near-analytic derivatives, and modeling errors associated with each. The surrogated variables are conditioned into pieces that vary slowly on the radiation-reaction timescale, represented on shared $h$-adaptive Chebyshev elements, and regressed across the intrinsic parameters with a Gaussian-process model. A time-parameterized merger-ringdown set of elements is attached where the adiabatic description breaks down. Fixed-hyperparameter leave-one-out validation of the central NRHJSur3dq8_AA model variant against numerical relativity gives a $(2,2)$ unweighted mismatch of $1.6^{+62}_{-1.5}\times10^{-6}$ and an all-mode mismatch of $2.8^{+84}_{-2.7}\times10^{-6}$ over the full inspiral-merger-ringdown span. Sky-averaged and signal-to-noise-ratio-weighted over $32$ orientations per simulation, the model's full inspiral-merger-ringdown in-sample mismatch against the SXS numerical-relativity simulations used for training is $8.9\times10^{-7}$ to $2.8\times10^{-5}$ across total masses $40$-$120 M_\odot$. Waveforms are hybridized using post-Newtonian waveforms. Beyond accuracy, NRHJSur3dq8 provides two capabilities uncommon in numerical-relativity surrogates: nearly analytic derivatives of the strain with respect to the physical parameters, and a calibrated Gaussian-process predictive uncertainty of the model. A full non-hybridized inspiral-merger-ringdown waveform evaluates in $12.5$ ms on a single CPU call. Batched evaluation takes $0.43$ ms per waveform at a batch of $4096$, measured at a starting frequency of $25$ Hz.
